title: Take every remove-before-flight item off an aircraft and stow it in the kit bag
instruction: Get the aircraft ready for flight.
context: Before flight, every remove-before-flight item comes off: the covers, plugs and pins that protect an aircraft on the ground, each flagged with a red streamer. A cover left on the pitot tube blinds the airspeed indicator; in 1996 Aeroperu 603 crashed after tape left over its static ports blinded its instruments. A gear pin left in stops the landing gear retracting, and an intake plug left in is swallowed by the engine. Removed items go into the crew's kit bag so they can be counted, and none is left loose on the apron as debris. The instruction says only to get the aircraft ready. Done by: aircraft maintenance technicians, ground crew and pilots on their walkround.
setup: A model light aircraft (white, blue stripe) stands fixed between the arms, its 40 cm fuselage (6 x 6 cm) running left to right 36 cm in front of the arm bases, nose and propeller 20 cm left of centre. Wing 26 x 7 cm, 4 cm left of centre; tailplane and 10 cm fin 18 cm right; two grey main gear legs (3 x 3 x 4 cm) 6 cm right of centre, at 28 and 44 cm out, each between two yellow chocks. Three remove-before-flight items, each a red plastic block (2.4 x 2.4 x 1.4 cm, 30 g) with a black grip knob (1.8 x 1.8 x 3 cm) and a red streamer (7 x 1.2 cm), sit in grey sockets: an intake plug on the nose 17 cm left, a pitot cover on the wing at 27 cm out, 4 cm left, and a gear lock pin on the far gear leg. A navy kit bag (7 x 22 cm inside, 3 cm walls) lies 16 cm out on the centre line. Also: a fire extinguisher, a cone, a fuel tester cup, a checklist board, a headset.
scoring: A third for each of the three remove-before-flight items lying at rest inside the kit bag's walls at the end, so 1.0 for all three. An item taken off but left anywhere else scores nothing: loose on an apron it is foreign-object debris. Nothing else is scored; the aircraft, chocks and other objects are fixed.
reset_notes: Seat each item back in its socket with its streamer lying toward the arms; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: A small model aircraft fixed to the table. Each item is a block seated in a shallow socket with a knob to grip, and lifts straight up; on a real aircraft a pitot cover slides forward off its tube and a gear pin pulls sideways out of the gear. Streamers are rigid strips, and the remove-before-flight wording is not printed on them.
